clue.text: Opera featuring Frenchwoman and monarch?

parts.note: Madame is the French title for a married woman
the monarch is a large orange and black butterfly

explanation.surface: A question about an opera starring a Frenchwoman and a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monarch' suggests a king or queen, but here it is the butterfly of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's famous opera about a Japanese bride bears this title.

clue.text: First man to market water

parts.note: Adam is the first man in the Bible
a sale is the act of marketing or selling goods

explanation.surface: The first man sets out to sell water.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular old idiom for plain drinking water, as the only drink Adam had.

clue.text: Jenny used to be in service

definitions.meaning: a jenny is the familiar name for the small brown bird
a member of the former Women's Royal Naval Service, now merged into the Royal Navy, was called this

explanation.surface: A woman called Jenny was once a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in service' suggests domestic service; it is the naval service, the WRNS, abolished as a separate body in 1993.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is commonly called Jenny, and a member of the old women's navy carried the same nickname.

clue.text: It's dangerous to ruin her plans

indicators.note: to ruin the plans is to wreck their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that wrecking a woman's plans is risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragments of an exploding shell are a danger to anyone nearby, so this is something hazardous.

clue.text: Metal shares are bargains, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the bargains word is to be taken by sound

parts.note: steals are bargains, things bought very cheaply

explanation.surface: An investor notes that metal-industry shares are cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: On the stock market, shares in steel companies are referred to by this plural.

clue.text: 8's is 2

parts.note: a bare arithmetic statement: the number which multiplied by itself three times makes eight is two

explanation.surface: A terse piece of arithmetic about the numbers eight and two.
explanation.definitionFit: Two times two times two is eight, so two is the third root of eight.

clue.text: In distress, appellant revoked claim

indicators.note: revoked is taken as called back, so the run is read backwards
In says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A distressed appellant withdraws a legal claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' takes TRESSA from 'distress, appellant', and 'revoked' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To claim something is to state it firmly as true, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Announcement about split in branch of US government

indicators.note: the announcement word goes about, around, the split word

parts.note: a statement is an announcement
to split is slang for to depart, leave

explanation.surface: A declaration about a rift inside a US government department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' looks like a noun for a rift; it is the verb meaning leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The US ministry for foreign affairs is officially known by this name.

clue.text: Heard lots about garrison town

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Rumours circulate about a military town.
explanation.walkthrough: ALDERSHOT is a Hampshire town, the traditional home of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: This English town is famous as the home of the British Army, a garrison town.

clue.text: Completely ready for trouble

parts.note: up means completely, as in eat up or used up
set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: Someone fully prepared for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone is to distress or disturb them, a synonym verb.

clue.text: Folk song about Asian country

indicators.note: the song goes about, around, the folk

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
folk are people, men

explanation.surface: A folk song concerning a country in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folk song' reads as one phrase, a traditional tune; the two words do separate jobs, and 'about' wraps one round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: This Caucasus republic is classed as a country of western Asia.

clue.text: Group in which one feels happiest?

definitions.text: Group in which one feels happiest?

parts.words: Group in which one feels happiest?
parts.note: plays on being in one's natural surroundings, read literally as a chemical group or a class of things

explanation.surface: A question about the circle of people one is happiest with.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'in your element' means where you feel most at home; the word also means a group or class.
explanation.definitionFit: An element can be a group or section, and one's natural sphere is where one is most content.

clue.text: Starts to encourage Left to adopt extremely authoritarian style

indicators.note: to adopt is to take on, so the extreme letters are added on
the starts to the next two words are their first letters
extremely gives the extremes, the first and last letters, of authoritarian

explanation.surface: Encouraging the Left to take up an authoritarian manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' gives E and L; 'extremely' gives AN, the first and last letters of 'authoritarian', which 'adopt' adds on.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair or verve is a kind of style, and this French borrowing names that dash.

clue.text: Irritated seducer, not being alone

indicators.note: irritated suggests the letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An annoyed seducer finds himself unaccompanied.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without a companion or chaperone is by themselves, so alone.

clue.text: Lutenist endlessly played instrument

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are performed in a new order
endlessly removes the final letter of the lutenist word

explanation.surface: A lute player keeps playing an instrument without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last T from 'Lutenist', and 'played' rearranges LUTENIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is an implement or tool, which is a sense of instrument.

clue.text: Unsportsmanlike behaviour seen at winter games?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, taunting a batsman to put him off is called this
riding sledges in the snow is a winter pastime

explanation.surface: Cheating spotted at the Winter Olympics.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, verbal abuse of the batsman is known by this name; the second sense is literal sledge riding.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both baiting an opponent in cricket and sliding about on sledges.

clue.text: Wandering with parent in Belgium

indicators.note: wandering means straying, so the letters move about

explanation.surface: Travelling with a parent in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: This port city lies in Belgium, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: Girl taken aback by grisly story

indicators.note: taken aback is read as taken backwards, so the girl's name is reversed

parts.note: Ella is a girl's name
gory means grisly, bloody

explanation.surface: A girl is shocked by a gruesome tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise or shock, but it signals reading the girl's name backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story with a hidden moral or political meaning.

clue.text: Old chancer used to go a bit too far

indicators.note: used suggests the letters are worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: An old rogue used to overstep the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to intrude beyond proper limits, going further than allowed.

clue.text: Naughty boy's a ringer for Peter's friend

parts.note: a tinker is a mischievous child, in British usage
a bell is something that rings

explanation.surface: A mischievous lad is the double of Peter's pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringer' suggests a lookalike; it is a bell. In Britain a tinker is a little rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy companion of Peter Pan in J M Barrie's story goes by this name.

clue.text: Girl's written about leader of Japanese assassins

indicators.note: the girl's name is written around the next letter

parts.note: Nina is a girl's name, with the possessive giving NINAS

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A girl writes about the chief of Japanese killers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of' gives J, which 'written about' puts inside NINAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese covert agents trained in espionage and killing were assassins.

clue.text: Barium compound found in rock

parts.note: Ba is the chemical symbol for barium
a salt is a chemical compound

explanation.surface: A barium compound is detected in a rock sample.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic rock.

clue.text: Some victims carry permanent emotional damage

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some victims are left with lasting trauma.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasting mark of emotional trauma is described as this, by analogy with a wound.

clue.text: Greens worked to protect last of pristine deserts

indicators.note: to protect is to surround, so the letters go around the final letter
worked means kneaded into a new shape, rearranging the letters
the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Environmentalists campaign to protect untouched deserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserts' looks like sandy wastes but is a verb, to abandon. 'worked' makes GRENES of 'Greens'; 'last of' gives E, put inside by 'to protect'.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise, deserting it.

clue.text: Finally giving you permission and space to make a mess

indicators.note: finally picks out the final letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: room means space

explanation.surface: At last you are allowed space to make a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' suggests untidiness; it is a dining room on a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: On a warship the junior officers eat in this room, so it is a naval mess.

clue.text: Blue and white flowers

parts.note: reads like a description of blooms but describes a river formed by Blue and White branches, one that flows

explanation.surface: Describes some pretty blue and white blossoms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' means things that flow, rivers; the Blue and White tributaries join at Khartoum.
explanation.definitionFit: This African river is formed by two branches named after the colours blue and white.

clue.text: King, knight and master

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's king
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A king, a knight and a master gathered together.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a skill is to acquire it fully, a synonym verb.

clue.text: Call round by arrangement to see elusive chap

indicators.note: by arrangement means the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Visit by appointment to meet a man who is hard to find.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD LUCAN is the British peer who vanished in 1974 after a murder and has never been found.
explanation.definitionFit: The fugitive peer, missing since 1974, is the byword for someone who cannot be found.
